verdictBasis: 1 blocker, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: Five of the six claimed repairs land, several of them exactly as the frozen findings specified. filesystemMeasurementTarget is a real new block computed before profile selection, resolutionPredicate is reordered around it, the Linux observation is bound to the resolving process's mount namespace with the longest-prefix and last-in-file selection rule I asked for, both osFamilies fail closed, the mountinfo token is cited by separator rather than by ordinal, /usr/lib/os-release is put out of scope, SONAME-ABI is moved out of tags into a companions registry, sonameAbi is declared metadata that never changes allow/refuse, the conditional booking is replaced with an unconditional determination, and the live locator now names the block by its standing rather than by number. What survives is the first evidence bullet of PTCB-V7-B1 itself. The new target block says when to measure, how to read the interface, and what constraint the result must satisfy, but never designates which volume or path is measured: linux.recordSelection needs 'the target path' and macos.interface needs 'the target volume', and the only definition offered — the host volume that will bind every relevant resolution — is a property over resolutions that computedWhen forbids observing yet. Separately, the sonameAbi retention repair names a loader-trace field, companionObservation, that the unchanged retained-event schema does not contain.

blockers.title: filesystemMeasurementTarget is ordered before selection but never designated: 'the target path' and 'the target volume' have no defined input

measurement.theOnlyDefinitionOffered: rule reads 'The host volume that will bind every relevant resolution on this profile. All relevant resolutions MUST satisfy this same target.' That is a property quantified over resolutions, not a designation of a volume.
measurement.theTimingConstraintItContradicts: computedWhen reads 'BEFORE platformProfile selection and independently of any later object resolution.' The volume that will bind every relevant resolution cannot be identified independently of those resolutions, so the definition cannot be evaluated at the time the contract requires the measurement to happen.
measurement.theMissingInput: linux.recordSelection selects 'the record whose mount-point field is the longest prefix of the target path'. No target path is defined anywhere. macos.interface reads 'struct statfs.f_fstypename of the target volume' and statfs takes a path argument that is likewise undefined. I searched the artifact for every occurrence of 'target', 'volume', 'install' and 'initial image': the only candidates are these clauses themselves plus originSearchPolicy.canonicalOrigin, which is a per-member declared origin, not a profile-level measurement target.
measurement.divergence: Two conforming verifiers on one host can take the target as the root mount, as the volume holding the signed closure, or as the volume holding the initial image. On a container or any host where those differ — an overlay root with the closure on a bind-mounted volume is the ordinary case — they read different mountinfo records, produce different OTHER-FSTYPE digests or different enum members, and compute different complete profile keys.

blockers.whyThisIsTheSameBlocker: PTCB-V7-B1's first evidence bullet reads 'The contract never designates which object or volume supplies the single filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution member before profile selection.' That sentence is still true of v8 word for word. The requiredRepair's other elements are delivered — a profile-level target defined before selection, a requirement that all relevant resolutions satisfy it, Linux observation bound to the resolving process and mount namespace, an exact mount-record selection algorithm, and fail-closed on missing or ambiguous selection — but the designation the evidence named is not.
blockers.consequence: Fail-closed rather than exploitable: divergent members produce refusals rather than substitutions. But the required member that gates allowlist freeze is still not reproducible across verifiers, which is what makes this a blocker rather than a gap.
blockers.requiredRepair: Designate the target by construction rather than by property. Name the path whose volume is measured — for example the signed closure's install root as delivered under exact-byte delivery — and derive the target from it, so the measurement has an input at the time computedWhen requires. Keep rule's all-relevant-resolutions clause as the enforced constraint and state that a host on which any relevant resolution falls outside the designated target refuses, which is the behaviour resolutionPredicate step 3 already implies.

shouldFix.title: The sonameAbi retention is routed to a loader-trace field that the retained-event schema does not define

measurement.theClaim: Three rostered clauses state the retention: 'The observation is retained on the loader-trace event as companionObservation' in the companions entry, and 'Retained as companionObservation' in both payload companions. honestyRepairsFromV7[2] repeats it.
measurement.theSchema: loaderTraces is byte-identical to v7 and is correctly absent from the roster. Its retainedEventSchema is a flat list of fourteen field names — eventTime, sequenceAndClosure, runIdentity, processIdentityAndParentage, subjectDigest, completePlatformProfileKey, allowlistOrCarrierDigest, taxonomyClass, taggedEvidenceForm, eventKind, resolvedObjectIdentity, route, allowlistMatch, enforcedOutcome. companionObservation is not among them, and the token occurs nowhere in loaderTraces.
measurement.againstTheFrozenRequirement: PTCB-V7-S1's requiredRepair reads 'If sonameAbi is metadata only, say presence/absence/mismatch never changes allow/refuse and state how it is retained.' The first half is delivered emphatically and consistently in four places. The second half names a field rather than provisioning one, so an implementer building traces from retainedEventSchema retains nothing and the stated retention does not occur.

shouldFix.consequence: The compatibility observation the contract promises to keep is not kept, so the metadata-only choice loses the evidence trail that made it acceptable instead of a refusal rule. No allow/refuse outcome changes, which is why this is not a blocker.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add companionObservation to retainedEventSchema, with whatever presence rule applies to non-libc events, and roster /loaderTraces in that successor. If loaderTraces is to stay frozen, say instead that the observation is retained alongside the trace and name where.

advisories.detail: The field opens 'Standing pin-rotation rule: each successor retains at least the immediate predecessor round and the current round in appliesFindingsOf; earlier rounds recover via basedOn', which is the repair, and then closes with the superseded v7 sentence verbatim: 'Standing pin-rotation rule: each successor retains the immediate predecessor round in appliesFindingsOf; earlier rounds recover via basedOn. My own CLAUDE-V7-ADV-2 rested on the exclusive reading, and the new sentence answers it, so I am not sustaining that finding — this is an editing residue in the same field, not a live contradiction.
advisories.suggestedFix: Delete the trailing superseded sentence, keeping its final clause about honestyRepairsFromV4 attached to the current rule.

coordinatorNote: v8 is close. The reordering of resolutionPredicate around a pre-selection measurement target is the right shape for Codex's blocker, the Linux selection algorithm and fail-closed rules are exactly what the frozen findings specified, and four separate advisories of mine were repaired structurally rather than cosmetically — SONAME-ABI moved to a real companions registry, the live locator now names a block by standing so it survives future successors, the mountinfo token is cited by separator rather than ordinal, and /usr/lib/os-release is settled by decision. That is PTCB-V7-B1's first evidence bullet, still true word for word, so I have sustained it as a blocker rather than downgrading it. The retention half of the sonameAbi repair names companionObservation, which the unchanged fourteen-field retained-event schema does not contain, so the promised evidence trail does not exist. I also record three misses of my own from v7, since the coordinator should weigh my grading accordingly: Codex saw the pre-selection ordering defect that I graded only as a failure-behaviour and record-selection gap; Codex caught the conditional booking that my own CLAUDE-V6-S3 minimum repair had demanded and that I did not re-check; and I considered the sonameAbi compatibility-outcome gap at v7 and judged it noise, where Codex graded it SHOULD-FIX and v8's four-place repair shows it was substantive.
